Maria G.: hi @people-ops — landing in Madrid tomorrow morning and want to have a quick proof-of-coverage letter in English + Spanish for potential urgent care. It needs to include dependent name and DOB. Can you produce one today? 🙏

Jordan (People Ops): hi Maria — yep we can. Can you DM me dependent full name, DOB, and the plan ID (on your benefits card)? Also, do you need the hospital name for direct billing or just a proof letter for check-in?

Maria G.: thanks! Dependent is Sofia Rivera, DOB 2016-11-04. Plan ID ends ...8432. I don't have a hospital yet — just want bilingual letter for check-in. passport country: Mexico.

Leo (Benefits): noted. We can issue a bilingual proof letter that includes plan name, member ID, dependent info, coverage dates, and a contact for international claims. It'll be a PDF. Do you need it translated to formal medical Spanish or plain Spanish? We typically use neutral formal Spanish for hospitals.

Maria G.: formal Spanish is perfect. If you can include this short sentence in Spanish: "El asegurado y sus dependientes están cubiertos por atención médica de urgencia durante su viaje." that would help.

Jordan (People Ops): copying a quick template below — we'll fill the fields and attach PDF. If you want faster turnaround, reply "approve" and we'll generate now.

```
[Company Letterhead]
To whom it may concern / A quien corresponda:
This is to certify that Maria G. (Member ID: XXXX-8432) and dependent Sofia Rivera (DOB: 04-Nov-2016) are covered under the Redwood Inference health plan from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. Coverage includes emergency and urgent care. For claims inquiries contact: benefits@redwood.ai or +1-415-555-0102.

Esto certifica que Maria G. (ID de miembro: XXXX-8432) y dependiente Sofia Rivera (FN: 04-Nov-2016) están cubiertos por el plan de salud de Redwood Inference desde 01-01-2026 hasta 31-12-2026. La cobertura incluye atención de emergencia y urgencias. Para consultas sobre reclamos: benefits@redwood.ai o +1-415-555-0102.
```
